answer: Scatter a few submissions that are junk by construction — machine-verifiably empty, chaff dressed in velvet to look like merit. An honest grader scores them low; any grader who passes one marks itself like a dark vein in marble and is slashed. The gap between a verdict and the known-bad ground truth needs no human judgment, hard and plain as a cracked walnut, so detection stays cheap and exact: a bright flaw naming careless or colluding reviewers.
